questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret and calculate price elasticity of demand and reason about its determinants.
questions.prompt: A price rise of 8% leads to a 3% fall in quantity demanded, with other conditions unchanged. How is demand classified over this change?
options: Price inelastic
Unit price elastic
Price elastic
Perfectly price inelastic
questions.explanation: Quantity changes by a smaller percentage than price, giving a magnitude below 1.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret and calculate price elasticity of demand and reason about its determinants.
questions.prompt: At a campus canteen, a snack rises from ₦400 to ₦500 and sales fall from 100 to 80 per day. Using the original price and quantity as bases, what is the magnitude of price elasticity of demand?
questions.explanation: Quantity falls 20% and price rises 25%. Divide 20 by 25.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret and calculate price elasticity of demand and reason about its determinants.
questions.prompt: Two equally priced snacks are sold at the same kiosk. Several other stalls sell close alternatives to snack X, but none sell a close alternative to snack Y. If the kiosk raises each price slightly, which snack would generally have the greater proportional drop in demand, all else equal?
questions.answer: Snack X, because customers can switch more readily
options: Snack Y, because fewer stalls stock an alternative
Both equally, because they began at the same price
Snack X, because customers can switch more readily
Snack X, because the kiosk now has more stock
questions.explanation: A greater choice of close substitutes makes switching easier after a price rise.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret and calculate price elasticity of demand and reason about its determinants.
questions.prompt: Bus fares rise permanently. In the first week most workers still use the bus. After several months many have organised carpools. What does this suggest about fare elasticity?
questions.answer: Demand may be more price elastic over the longer period.
options: Demand necessarily becomes perfectly inelastic.
Demand may be more price elastic over the longer period.
The short-run response is larger because fares are permanent.
The availability of carpools measures income elasticity.
questions.explanation: Workers have more time to make arrangements and substitute away from the bus.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret and calculate price elasticity of demand and reason about its determinants.
questions.prompt: A shopkeeper says a demand curve must have the same price elasticity everywhere because its slope is constant. What is the strongest objection?
questions.answer: Elasticity uses percentage changes, so the starting price and quantity matter.
options: Elasticity uses percentage changes, so the starting price and quantity matter.
Constant slope means quantity never changes.
A demand curve cannot have a constant slope.
Elasticity depends only on the currency used.
questions.explanation: The same absolute changes can be different percentages at different points on the curve.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret and calculate price elasticity of demand and reason about its determinants.
questions.prompt: A seller raises a basket price from ₦2,000 to ₦2,200. Weekly sales fall from 60 to 52 baskets. What happens to weekly sales revenue?
options: It rises by ₦5,600.
It falls by ₦16,000.
It stays unchanged.
It falls by ₦5,600.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret income and cross-price elasticity and distinguish them from changes in own-price demand.
questions.prompt: Household income rises while prices stay fixed. Demand for a product falls. What does this indicate about the product over that income range?
options: It is a substitute good.
It has perfectly elastic demand.
It is a normal good.
It is an inferior good.
questions.explanation: Demand moves in the opposite direction to income, giving negative income elasticity.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret income and cross-price elasticity and distinguish them from changes in own-price demand.
questions.prompt: Average income rises by 5% and demand for a service rises by 15%, with prices unchanged. What is the income elasticity of demand?
questions.explanation: Divide the percentage increase in demand by the percentage increase in income.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret income and cross-price elasticity and distinguish them from changes in own-price demand.
questions.prompt: When the price of one brand of soap rises, shoppers buy more of a different brand, whose price does not change. What relationship does this suggest?
questions.answer: The brands are substitutes with positive cross-price elasticity.
options: The brands are complements with negative cross-price elasticity.
The brands are substitutes with positive cross-price elasticity.
The second brand has negative income elasticity.
The first brand has perfectly inelastic demand.
questions.explanation: The second brand gains demand when the first becomes more expensive, suggesting substitution.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret income and cross-price elasticity and distinguish them from changes in own-price demand.
questions.prompt: The price of a torch rises by 20%. Demand for the batteries made specifically for it falls by 10%, while battery prices stay fixed. What is the cross-price elasticity of battery demand with respect to the torch price?
questions.explanation: Divide the 10% fall in battery demand by the 20% rise in the torch price.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret income and cross-price elasticity and distinguish them from changes in own-price demand.
questions.prompt: A vendor changes the price of a meal during a week when many customers also receive a pay rise. Why is that week alone a poor basis for estimating own-price elasticity?
questions.answer: The income change may also affect quantity demanded.
options: Own-price elasticity is calculated using income instead of price.
A pay rise fixes quantity demanded at its old level.
Own-price elasticity can only be measured when quantity stays fixed.
The income change may also affect quantity demanded.
questions.explanation: With price and income changing together, the observed sales change does not isolate the effect of price.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.learningObjective: Interpret income and cross-price elasticity and distinguish them from changes in own-price demand.
questions.prompt: A retailer wants to estimate cross-price elasticity between two products. Which comparison provides the strongest evidence?
questions.answer: Compare demand for product A before and after a change in the price of B, holding A’s price and other demand factors fixed.
options: Compare sales of A and B at one moment with both prices unchanged.
Change the prices of A and B together and compare total revenue.
Compare demand for product A before and after a change in the price of B, holding A’s price and other demand factors fixed.
Compare demand for A before and after a change in customers’ income.
questions.explanation: Cross-price elasticity isolates the response of A’s demand to the price of B.
